issues.description: The solution repository implements SpaceGoat, SpacePig, and SpaceSeal classes instead of the Goat, Pig, and Seal classes declared in the problem statement and referenced in the template. In the solution, Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java are present but empty. This name/type mismatch (and missing implementations for the expected class names) creates confusion about the intended class names and prevents directly using the provided solution classes to satisfy the exercise specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Either provide concrete implementations for Goat, Pig, and Seal in the solution repository that match the problem specification (constructors and methods as described), or rename the SpaceGoat, SpacePig, and SpaceSeal classes to Goat, Pig, and Seal (and update their return strings accordingly). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to explicitly require the Space-prefixed class names—ensure names are consistent across problem, template, and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to animal classes named Goat, Pig, and Seal (the core conceptual entities students must implement). The solution repository instead provides classes named SpaceGoat, SpacePig, and SpaceSeal implementing the same behavior. This introduces a cross-artifact identifier naming inconsistency: students reading the problem/template expect classes Goat/Pig/Seal but the reference solution uses different names (Space*), making it harder to map requirements to the provided solution and increasing unnecessary cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution's class names with the problem/template by renaming SpaceGoat, SpacePig, and SpaceSeal to Goat, Pig, and Seal respectively (or add thin wrapper classes Goat/Pig/Seal that delegate to the Space* implementations). Ensure the solution repository exposes the same class identifiers used in the problem statement and template to remove the mapping barrier.
